decisive_items: a painless ulcer on the prepuce
a disseminated maculopapular rash on the trunk and extremities
painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes (up to 3 cm)
response.rationale: Classic secondary syphilis triad: healing chancre, maculopapular rash, painless lymphadenopathy, with high lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis and extreme leukocytosis; prior treated syphilis does not exclude reinfection. R6 is the same entity but less specific.

rejected.why: HHV-6 lacks chancre and typical secondary syphilis pattern; extreme leukocytosis not characteristic.
HHV-8 usually Kaposi sarcoma or effusion lymphoma; no supporting skin/lymph node pattern.
Lymphoma could cause lymphadenopathy and leukocytosis but rash and chancre history favor syphilis.
Infectious mononucleosis can mimic but painless genital ulcer and prior syphilis history point to syphilis.
CMV in immunocompetent/controlled HIV less likely; no specific CMV features.
Toxoplasmosis typically focal CNS signs, not this rash/ulcer pattern; CD4 high.
IRIS requires recent immune recovery; CD4 high and undetectable viral load, no temporal trigger.
